questions.stem: Where do the nitrogen and oxygen that form NOx in car engines come from?

options.text: From the air drawn into the engine
options.explanation: Air is roughly four-fifths nitrogen and one-fifth oxygen, and engine heat welds them together.

options.text: From the petrol molecules themselves
options.explanation: Hydrocarbons carry no nitrogen; the gases come from the air the engine breathes.

options.text: From the catalytic converter
options.explanation: The converter cleans exhaust gases; it is not the source of the nitrogen oxides.

options.text: From the sulfur impurities in the fuel
options.explanation: Sulfur impurities produce SO2, a separate pollutant family.

questions.stem: What condition inside an engine allows nitrogen and oxygen to react?

options.text: The very high temperature and pressure reached there
options.explanation: Ordinary air is unreactive; only engine-level heat and pressure push the two gases together.

options.text: The cold of the exhaust pipe
options.explanation: Cold ends the chemistry; the reaction happens in the hot combustion chamber.

options.text: The presence of water in the fuel line
options.explanation: Water plays no part in forming nitrogen oxides.

options.text: A spark plug made of platinum
options.explanation: The spark ignites fuel; it is the temperature and pressure that form NOx.

questions.stem: Balance the equation for sulfur burning: S + O2 -> ?

options.text: SO2
options.explanation: One sulfur atom joins two oxygen atoms, the exact recipe for sulfur dioxide.

options.text: SO3
options.explanation: The trioxide needs a further step; direct burning gives the dioxide.

options.text: H2SO4
options.explanation: Sulfuric acid forms later in rainwater; the flame product is the dioxide gas.

options.text: S2O
options.explanation: That formula matches neither the atom counts nor the named product.

questions.stem: Why does sulfur dioxide appear in the exhaust of a petrol car at all?

options.text: Because the fuel carries sulfur impurities that burn with it
options.explanation: The combustion of the impurity is the route; no petrol molecule contains sulfur by design.

options.text: Because nitrogen in air reacts with sulfur
options.explanation: Air nitrogen heads down the NOx route; the sulfur burns with oxygen instead.

options.text: Because the converter manufactures it from clean gases
options.explanation: Converters destroy pollutants; they do not create sulfur dioxide.

options.text: Because sulfur dissolves from engine oil into the exhaust
options.explanation: The route is the burning fuel impurity, not oil leaching.

questions.stem: Besides acid rain, which adverse effects do nitrogen oxides have?

options.text: Photochemical smog and breathing difficulties for people with asthma
options.explanation: The note lists smog and asthma-linked breathing trouble alongside acid rain.

options.text: They dye surfaces black with soot
options.explanation: Soot belongs to incomplete burning of fuel, not to nitrogen oxides.

options.text: They cool the engine cylinders
options.explanation: Engine cooling is unrelated to exhaust chemistry.

options.text: They have no effects beyond acid rain
options.explanation: Smog and breathing effects are explicit in the note.

questions.stem: Which acid forms when sulfur dioxide dissolves in rainwater with oxygen?

options.text: Sulfuric acid
options.explanation: The balanced route 2SO2 + O2 + 2H2O -> 2H2SO4 names the acid directly.

options.text: Nitric acid
options.explanation: Nitric acid belongs to the nitrogen dioxide route, not the sulfur one.

options.text: Hydrochloric acid
options.explanation: No chlorine is present anywhere in this story.

options.text: Carbonic acid
options.explanation: Carbonic acid comes from carbon dioxide in water, a different gas.

questions.stem: What mixture forms when nitrogen dioxide reacts with rain water?

options.text: A mixture of nitrous and nitric acids
options.explanation: The equation 2NO2 + H2O -> HNO2 + HNO3 delivers one of each acid.

options.text: Sulfuric acid only
options.explanation: Sulfuric acid is the sulfur dioxide route; NO2 makes the two nitrogen acids.

options.text: Nitrogen gas and hydrogen gas
options.explanation: The reaction makes acids, not free gases.

options.text: Only nitric acid, with nothing else
options.explanation: The note is explicit that a mixture of nitrous and nitric acids forms.

questions.stem: Which event, besides engines, can trigger nitrogen oxide formation in air?

options.text: Lightning strikes
options.explanation: The note records lightning as a natural trigger for nitrogen monoxide and dioxide formation.

options.text: Rainfall on limestone
options.explanation: That is a weathering story, not a nitrogen oxide source.

options.text: Volcanic sulfur release
options.explanation: Volcanoes feed the sulfur family; lightning feeds the nitrogen one.

options.text: Plant photosynthesis
options.explanation: Photosynthesis consumes carbon dioxide and releases oxygen; it makes no NOx.

questions.stem: Which damage is caused by acid rain according to the note?

options.text: Corrosion of metal structures and carbonate statues
options.explanation: The note lists corrosion of metals, buildings and carbonate rock among the impacts.

options.text: It strengthens concrete buildings
options.explanation: Acid attack weakens and corrodes; nothing is strengthened.

options.text: It bleaches the colour from fabrics only
options.explanation: Fabric bleaching is not in the damage list; crops, water and lungs are.

options.text: It has no effect on living things
options.explanation: Damage to aquatic organisms and irritation of lungs and eyes are explicit.

questions.stem: How do the acid droplets eventually reach the ground?

options.text: Cloud droplets grow heavier as they rise and cool, then fall as rain
options.explanation: The note tracks droplets growing with cooling until they are heavy enough to fall as acid rain.

options.text: The acids fall as dry powder from the clouds
options.explanation: The acids travel dissolved in water droplets, not as powder.

options.text: They sink to the ground as heavy gas
options.explanation: The delivery is rainfall, not a gas pouring downhill.

options.text: They never reach the ground at all
options.explanation: Falling as acid rain is the entire point of the formation story.
